tasks.short: Prepare the program's slides and handouts, arrange dates and sign-ups, give the sessions on classroom management or parenting skills, and collect evaluations.

steps.what: School psychologist prepares slides and handouts for educational programs
School psychologist arranges dates and sign-ups by e-mail
School psychologist provides educational programs on classroom management or parenting skills
School psychologist collects paper evaluations and types them up

tasks.design: Program materials are kept in a shared library by topic and audience ({DOCS}) and adapted per group rather than built each time. Teachers and parents sign up through an online form instead of e-mail. Evaluations are collected with a QR form at the end of the session, so nothing is typed up. Giving the sessions stays with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were built per session, sign-ups handled by e-mail and evaluations typed from paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared libraries, sign-up forms and QR evaluation forms are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Each school wants its own examples.
tasks.human_edge: Answering a teacher's hardest classroom story with a practical idea.

evidence.claim: Sign-up forms and QR evaluation forms are standard tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the program request to evaluations collected; program funding is outside.
Input contract: materials in the library; fallback is building them per session.
Participants sign up online in about the time an e-mail took; a little participant time is priced.

incremental.description: School psychologist keeps the material library current.
Teachers and parents sign up and fill evaluations online.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off programs; high: repeated programs for many schools.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review students' assessments and support plans, design class adaptations and programs with teachers, write the program plan per student, and discuss it with parents.

steps.what: School psychologist reviews special students' assessments and support plans
School psychologist designs classes and programs with teachers to meet the needs of special students
School psychologist writes the program plan per student
School psychologist discusses the plan with parents

tasks.design: A student view in the school's student system ({OTHER}) shows assessments, support plans and progress together, so the psychologist does not open several files. The program plan uses a template whose goals link to the assessment findings. Designing programs with teachers and discussing plans with parents stay with the psychologist; no software decides on special-needs support.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessments and plans sat in several files, and plans were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Student systems show assessments and plans in one view.
tasks.still_hard: Outside reports arrive as scanned letters.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the adaptation that lets a child join the class again.

evidence.claim: Student systems can show assessments, support plans and progress in one view.
AI that decides on special-needs eligibility may be high-risk; here no software decides.

assumptions: Boundary: from student needs to the plan discussed; funding decisions are outside.
Input contract: assessments stored in the student system; fallback is files.
research_questions: Is preparation time per plan shorter?

incremental.description: School psychologist scans outside reports into the student view.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few special students; high: many plans per year.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search and screen the literature, design the study, collect data in schools, code open answers and interviews, and analyse and write up the research.

steps.what: School psychologist searches and screens literature on learning and behavior issues

loop.input: Titles and abstracts from the database search.
loop.output: Records ordered with the most likely relevant first.
loop.check: The psychologist screens every record shown; a sample of unscreened records is checked before stopping.
loop.stop: Stop after a set number of irrelevant records in a row, then check the sample.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevance does not follow keywords; reading all records takes weeks.

steps.what: School psychologist conducts research by collecting data in schools
School psychologist codes open answers and interview transcripts

loop.input: Transcripts and open answers and the study's codebook.
loop.check: The psychologist checks every AI-coded segment; a second coder double-codes a sample against an agreed agreement rate.
loop.stop: One pass per document; segments without a suggestion go to the psychologist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Children and teachers say the same thing in many ways; keyword rules miss them.

steps.what: School psychologist analyses the data and writes the findings

tasks.design: Literature screening uses an active-learning screener ({OTHER}) that shows the most likely relevant records first; the psychologist screens every record shown and checks a sample before stopping. Open answers and transcripts get suggested codes from the study's codebook in the qualitative analysis tool; the psychologist checks every coded segment and a second coder double-codes a sample. Designing the study, collecting data, analysing and writing stay with the psychologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every record was screened and every segment coded by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Active-learning screeners and code suggestion in qualitative tools exist.
tasks.still_hard: Suggested codes drift from the codebook's meaning.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the research question that teachers actually need answered.
tasks.altitude: The psychologist checks screening and coding instead of doing all of it by hand.

reach.learn: Whether findings arrive in time to use.

evidence.claim: ASReview LAB puts likely relevant records first for screening.
In simulations on six review datasets, 63.9% to 91.7% fewer records were screened to find 95% of relevant ones.
MAXQDA suggests codes and advises a human check of every AI-coded segment.
Research on special-category data needs safeguards, and without consent four joint conditions.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to findings written; publication is outside.
Input contract: parental consent for research data; fallback is coding by hand.
The psychologist checks every screened record and coded segment.
research_questions: How often does the double-coder disagree with suggested codes?

already_counted.description: School psychologist screens records shown by the screener.

incremental.description: A second coder double-codes a sample.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small studies; high: large literature reviews and many interviews.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The school psychologist keeps teaching programs, designing support with teachers and doing research; building materials, file searches, full screening and hand coding shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A psychologist with more time for children and schools.
